newsitem.title: CHINA: CHINA 1998 GDP SEEN UP 11 PCT - OFFICIAL MAGAZINE.
newsitem.headline: CHINA 1998 GDP SEEN UP 11 PCT - OFFICIAL MAGAZINE.

text.p: China's economy is expected to grow at a faster rate in 1998 compared with this year, while inflation is forecast to be even lower, Outlook magazine said in its latest edition on Wednesday.
Gross Domestic Product (GDP) was forecast to grow 11 percent in 1998, the official weekly magazine agency said.

A recent study by the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, China's premier think-tank, and the State Statistical Bureau forecast GDP growth of 10 percent this year. The economy grew by 9.8 percent last year.
China's benchmark retail price inflation (RPI) would be two percent in 1998, Outlook said.

China has forecast RPI this year would be about 3.0-4.0 percent, revising an earlier target of 6.0 percent. RPI was 6.1 percent in 1996, down from 14.8 percent in 1995 and a communist-era high of 21.7 percent in 1994.
Exports would climb by about 20 percent next year and grain output would inch up about one percent, the magazine said. It gave no further details.
